evidence.claim: Product scope: persistent global joi, workbenches, local and A2A partners; cross-platform clients. The release guide requires stable version upgrades, generated notes and immutable published versions.

Layer responsibilities, one scheduler, durable inbox, policy-gated outbox and safe projections. The root tick schedules ordinary turns serially and independent goal syntheses concurrently with same-goal exclusion.

Electron lifecycle and window composition use isolated webPreferences and runtime worker client. An explicit development API port reaches the runtime before the Electron window loads Vite. The named Codex window hands approved HTTPS authorization links to the system browser. An explicitly retained isolated developer profile keeps its data across restarts and has a single-instance lock. The installed desktop shell presents verified updates and launches Windows NSIS after graceful runtime shutdown.

Scoped question answers and explicit conversation recovery use the same authenticated request layer. The existing goal detail endpoint accepts optional summary and map page views. Desktop-only update reads and versioned writes use the same authenticated HTTP client.

Conversation UI retains selectors, title editing, history pages and drafts. Scoped progress reads back off and cancel; reads and accepted SSE snapshots clear only their connection notice. Selection epochs and stream revisions reject stale success and failure callbacks. Safe execution failures remain distinct. LAN browsers reuse shared conversation controls without mounting desktop workspace/Git. Entering a narrow viewport closes history; phone history selection and new drafts close the drawer. Optional Settings and attachment transport capabilities keep unavailable controls out of the paired fallback. Enter and the send button share availability checks. Running turns display active feedback, and completed turn footers show the status and reply copy action. The selected transcript restores independently of configuration and history lists. Skills are read when opened, and send availability waits for applicable configuration. A completed reply can open a separate conversation with its initial configuration and an empty composer. Failed fork requests reuse the same identity. Sidebar groups and rows use local ordering while the composer still uses the workbench catalog. Question cards retain history and separate waitingForUser from execution status; arrival anchors the active card heading. Scoped answers refresh the relevant conversation, and explicit interrupted recovery uses the application endpoint. Answer receipts apply independently of refresh, and a shared SSE and polling revision rejects stale post-answer snapshots. Linked recovery completion updates the historical source card.
Desktop Git controls, safe parsed diff views, bounded workspace file previews and sandboxed explicit HTTP(S) browser frames.

Ordinary conversations bind turns to execution segments and treat current user intent as the task. Startup restores trustworthy Pi results by stable turn and segment identity without dispatching. Fork creation persists a selected-turn handoff without dispatching. The first submitted turn creates a fresh execution segment from that seed. Scoped question answers, stop/child cancellation and committed question observations reuse the durable service. Cold boot marks unconsumed cards interrupted. Explicit recovery uses one stable request per parent turn and complete private original-request/answer context, without fabricating tool results or replaying unknown effects. Only the selected unanswered interrupted card adopts its displayed default; other unanswered cards remain explicit requests to ask again, and cleanup is question-specific. Graceful host shutdown preserves INTERRUPTED rather than user-canceled ownership. Legacy pending-question text appends without replacing preceding output. Recovery retries use the prior attempt identity and preserve the original answer until successful settlement. Completed recovery updates include the original card projection for SSE readers.

SQLite binds running turns to stable execution segments, lists Pi recovery candidates and guards terminal updates. Public Pi history suppresses stale thinking summaries. An atomic fork binds a new identity to the source turn and workbench and stores the private handoff separately from public configuration. Parent-turn question joins preserve safe cards in current reads and historical pages; waitingForUser is separate from RUNNING. Private recovery context is stored and checked as part of submission identity, never returned in the public turn DTO. Recovery attempts link to their source turn in the submission transaction. Successful settlement acknowledges source answers in the same transaction as the result.
simple-git wraps installed Git with allowlisted commands and server-owned roots; path validation, staged-only commits, non-force sync and redacted text previews.

Conversations inherit a bounded owned Workbench projection and currently active learned method. Handoffs, settled recovery and child identities keep their private scopes. The same question service is injected into ConversationService and Pi; child requests use the child Work identity for durable question ownership. Graceful close supplies an explicit host-shutdown reason to children instead of treating shutdown as user cancellation.

Shared conversation DTOs expose safe committed turn updates, scoped history, timing and explicitly public provider summaries. An empty fork exposes only its initial configuration, with the private seed kept server-side. Turns optionally carry sanitized questions and waitingForUser without changing terminal state enums. A conversation update can carry the related original turn whose recovery receipts changed.

Independent conversations have no per-workbench, partner or global active-turn cap. Outbox batches renew per-delivery claims and drain on close; explicit Git remains serial and repository-coordinated.
